findings.title: Native window lookup and key events are dispatched from a background goroutine
findings.message: The check goroutine calls core.TheApp.WindowByName and native.Events().KeyChord directly, off the UI/main thread. The other state it touches is correctly marshalled through a.Do. Cogent Core's window list and event manager are not goroutine-safe, so this can race with the render loop. It may corrupt event ordering and make the smoke test flaky or crash.
findings.suggestion: Look up the windows and dispatch the synthetic key chords inside a.Do, or through whatever main-queue helper the driver provides. A small helper such as `sendChord(a, name, r, code, mods)` that wraps the lookup and the KeyChord call in a.Do would cover every call site.

findings.title: StopMain posts an empty event that may reach an already-terminated GLFW or a nil This
findings.message: StopMain now calls `a.This.SendEmptyEvent()` after closing MainDone, and it can be called more than once or after the loop has exited. On the desktop driver the loop calls `glfw.Terminate()` before returning, and a later StopMain would post an empty event to an uninitialised GLFW. That can panic or raise a GLFW error. `a.This` may also be nil if StopMain is called before it is set.
findings.suggestion: Guard the call with `if a.This != nil`. Make the desktop SendEmptyEvent a no-op once GLFW is terminated, for example with an atomic 'terminated' flag. Alternatively, skip the wake-up when the loop has already exited.

finding.title: Creating the whole window inside one main-queue callback risks self-deadlock
finding.message: NewWindow now runs the whole window-creation transaction inside one callback on the main loop. That includes the user hooks `system.UpdateLogicalDPIScaleFunc` and `a.NativeAttach`, and helpers such as `w.updateGeometry()` and `newGlfwWindow`. If any of these still call `a.RunOnMain` or `w.Show()`, `SetGeometry` or similar, they will block on `queue <- ...` while the loop is busy running this callback, which deadlocks. The new doc comment says this call pattern is forbidden, but nothing enforces it.
finding.suggestion: Audit everything reachable from newWindowOnMain, including UpdateLogicalDPIScaleFunc, NativeAttach, updateGeometry and newGlfwWindow, for RunOnMain/RunOnMainIfOpen calls and replace them with *OnMain variants. Alternatively, make RunOnMainIfOpen detect re-entrancy (for example with a main-thread flag) and run the function inline.
